coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fifteen attacks run, none landed. Custody is clean and the MF-6 is unapplied: 7c36b624 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 3c8dafb, file 08 still at 25 gate rows with no DR-G26, COORD at its pin, and all four file pins plus the D-151 commit pin reproducing. One custody note worth recording: when this review was first requested the dispatch and review prompt were not on disk and I declined to review the frozen draft without them; both appeared before the review ran and pin the digest the draft already carried, so nothing was reviewed outside an instrument. I verified the predecessor first — D-151's applied row and condition-4 cell are byte-identical to the blocks it consented to, condition 4 is still MET, and the non-gate rows and 4-of-32 figure are untouched. The mechanics hold. The before operand is byte-exact and occurs exactly once in the whole file; all three fenced blocks carry zero backslash bytes and no edge whitespace, which is the specific attack this prompt raised; and a character-by-character diff shows exactly five changes — 25 to 26 owners, 21 to 22 required gates, the D-152 attribution, the G26-named clause, and 22 to 23 OPEN — with the G03/G04, G17, G23, G24 and G25 clauses and the HARD-BLOCKED count untouched. Those figures reconcile against a table I counted myself. DR-G26 is free, the anchor is real, and Limb B names the identifier in the same act so condition 4 holds at 22 of 22. The one place this kind carries extra risk is G17, since it adds a SARIF-adjacent obligation on a surface D-077 dropped, so I gave it a separate audit: Limb A adds only DR-G26 and states G17 remains inapplicable, the entry refuses restoration in three places, the new row's own retained-evidence column carries 'G17 remains inapplicable', the after operand leaves the G17 clause untouched, and the live DR-G17 row still reads dropped and not required-now. No restoration and no required-now entry. Fidelity holds too: the owner string and the NT-5-only ownership match the artifact exactly, the row's claim is its first two claim sentences with the third relocated rather than dropped, the retained-evidence column tracks NT-5's contract input and pass, and three leftover classes is the correct count against all eight. Two items are recorded as considered and declined, including that the do-not-unwrite list drops D-148 relative to D-151's — a difference that widens no scope, on the same reasoning I used three times before.
